chapter: Willie Lynch, the Blue Rhythm Band and Teddy Hill
title: Joining Teddy Hill's band at the Savoy
summary: Teddy Hill hired him after the Blue Rhythm Band; Holmes lists the personnel including Blanchard, Pinkett, Sam Allen and Bill Beason, with Roy Eldridge replacing Pinkett.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So from there you went to Teddy Hill?
Yeah.
The tenor saxophone...

Teddy Hill was forming a band, or he had a band in the Savoy Ballroom... No, he was getting ready to go in the Savoy Ballroom. And he heard I had come' out of the Blue Rhythm Band. So he asked me if I wanted a job, and I said, "Sure." So I worked at the Savoy on numerous occasions.
And of course, you knew Teddy Hill from earlier work
with Henry Allen and Russell.
Oh, yeah, I mean, we'd worked with all them guys on... Yeah. He was at the Nest Club when I first met Russell.

So I go up to the Savoy with Teddy Hill, and there was Blanchard, a saxophone player in the band, Teddy Hill and myself -- we were the reed section. He had Ward Pinkett. Hmm, I've forgotten who the other one was. And somebody else, I don't know just exactly who it was.
There was one trombone you mentioned, but you can't remember who.
Yeah. I can't remember his name either.
And then Sam Allen on piano.
Sam Allen on piano. Uncle(?) Rick on bass.
Richard Fulbright.
And...
Bill Beason.

Bill Beason on drums. That's correct. And I don't know who was playing guitar, if it was John Smith or not. I think it was John Smith, but I'm not certain of that. Yeah, I think it was John Smith. But anyway...
You said Roy Eldridge came in shortly after...
Yeah, joined us a little later.
And replaced Pinkett.
I'm sure he replaced Pinkett, yes... Because something happened between Pinkett and Teddy, so he had to replace Pinkett.
Now, you actually went into the Savoy.
Oh, we were there. We were there. And Teddy stayed there for quite a while. He stayed there quite a while. Then when I came out, I think I went back with Luis Russell's band.
